title: Getting Everything You Can Out Of All You’ve Got

questions.q: What makes a Better-Than-Risk-Free guarantee different from a refund?
a: It also compensates customers for wasted time and effort
It doubles the length of a standard guarantee
It offers a replacement instead of money back
It covers only products bought in a store
questions.why: The first lesson says the guarantee returns the purchase price and then makes amends for the customer's trouble.

questions.q: Which businesses should you build alliances with?
a: Related businesses that are not direct competitors
The largest companies in your industry
Direct rivals selling similar products
Suppliers who set your prices
questions.why: The second lesson says partners need your product anyway and will not lose business by recommending you.

questions.q: Why do partner recommendations convert so well?
a: Customers already trust the business recommending you
Partners usually work for free
Partners always have bigger mailing lists
Partners share your exact target audience
questions.why: The second lesson says people are far more likely to buy from someone their trusted provider suggests.

questions.q: Which cross-selling example does the summary use for Amazon?
a: Showing picture frames with pictures, nails and a hammer
Bundling a phone with a case and charger
Recommending a printer after a laptop purchase
Offering a discount on repeat orders
questions.why: The second lesson says to spot what customers buy alongside your product and partner with those sellers.

questions.q: What does Abraham say about trading in business today?
a: Non-monetary trades can still create win-win deals
Bartering died out with modern currency
Trades only work between retailers
Trades must always involve equal cash value
questions.why: The third lesson's pizza, sushi and café example shows a three-way trade that gets everyone what they want.
